key_insight: The paper extends adversarial certification from risk-neutral RL to risk-sensitive RL by deriving tractable lower bounds on exponential utility under bounded state perturbations.
engineering_relevance: This gives safety-critical RL practitioners a way to certify worst-case performance when deployed under observation attacks or noisy state inputs.
method: Relax the adversarial perturbation set using a ϕ-divergence formulation.
Convert the certified risk-sensitive lower-bound problem into a convex program and derive its dual for tractable computation.
Use separate training risk-aversion β from evaluation risk level to improve certified bounds empirically.
evidence_signal: Experiments on OpenAI Gym tasks and a machine replacement problem show risk-averse training usually improves certified lower bounds, especially with larger perturbation budgets.
watch_item: Certification gains are non-monotonic in training risk aversion, so overly conservative policies can reduce the certified lower bound.
paper_title: Certifying Lower Bounds for Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning under Adversarial State Perturbations
